---
title: "Quantitative Genetics"
subtitle: "Foundations of Quantitative Trait Analysis"
---

## Course Overview

This course introduces the mathematical, statistical, and biological foundations used to study quantitative traits. It connects genetic and environmental sources of phenotypic variation with heritability, response to selection, and the genetic architecture of complex traits.

## Learning Objectives

After completing the course, students should be able to:

- Describe quantitative variation using means, variances, and distributions.
- Explain how genetic and environmental effects contribute to phenotypic variation.
- Distinguish additive, dominance, and environmental variance components.
- Calculate and interpret broad-sense and narrow-sense heritability.
- Explain response to selection and the breeder's equation.
- Relate quantitative-genetics concepts to complex-trait analysis and breeding.

## Prerequisites

- Basic genetics and Mendelian inheritance
- Introductory statistics
- Basic familiarity with R

## Course Materials

Start with the [course map](tutorials/course_map.qmd) for prerequisites, R requirements and routes through the population-genetics and quantitative-genetics practicals.

- [Quantitative Genetics slides](slides/introduction_quantitative_genetics.html)
- [Narrated Quantitative Genetics slides](slides/introduction_quantitative_genetics_narrated.html)

- [Practical 1: Exploring quantitative traits in a mouse population](tutorials/mouse_quantitative_traits.qmd) — guided R analysis, figures, interpretation questions and solutions.

- [Practical 2: From genotype effects to quantitative variation](tutorials/mouse_single_locus.qmd) — allele frequencies, genotype contrasts and single-locus variance.

- [Practical 3: Estimating genetic parameters](tutorials/mouse_genetic_parameters.qmd) — pedigree relationships, REML and heritability.
- [Practical 4: Predicting pedigree breeding values](tutorials/mouse_pedigree_breeding_values.qmd) — BLUP, shrinkage and reliability.
- [Practical 5: Predicting genomic breeding values](tutorials/mouse_genomic_breeding_values.qmd) — genomic relationships and held-out phenotype prediction.

- [Practical 6: Breeding objectives and selection indices](tutorials/breeding_objectives_indices.qmd) — economic weights, covariance inputs and expected response.

- [Practical 7: Selection policies and mating plans](tutorials/selection_mating_plans.qmd) — eligibility, quotas, parent contributions and random versus balanced mating.

- [Practical 8: Simulating selection response](tutorials/simulating_selection_response.qmd) — offspring inheritance, fixed-base gain and marker diversity.

- [Practical 9: Relationships, mating and inbreeding](tutorials/relationships_mating_inbreeding.qmd) — parental kinship, equal contributions and offspring inbreeding.

- [Practical 10: Validating predictions and selection decisions](tutorials/validating_selection_predictions.qmd) — family splits, training-only fitting, calibration and shortlist outcomes.

- [Practical 11: Comparing breeding programmes](tutorials/comparing_breeding_programmes.qmd) — a capstone on recording policies, paired outcomes, gain, diversity and costs.

- [Practical 12: Genotype-by-environment interaction and heritability](tutorials/genotype_environment_heritability.qmd) — reaction norms, replicated trials and broad-sense entry-mean heritability.
